subject: Observability onboarding: setup runway, ownership grid, and alert triage cadence
messages:

Subject: Observability onboarding: setup runway, ownership grid, and alert triage cadence

Hi Samir —

Good to meet this week. As discussed on the call, we want to set a concise 3-week runway to get Northgate's core observability stack in place so your SREs can triage quickly during the pilot. Key goals for phase 1:

- Dashboard baseline for API and inference latency + error rate
- Tracing hooks on the client and server spans for request id propagation
- Error taxonomy that maps service errors to triage owners and PagerDuty escalation policy
- Alert routing for high-severity incidents and a customer-facing runbook in the shared binder

I've attached a draft ownership grid and a simple alert-routing diagram to get us started. Proposed cadence: weekly 60-min check-ins (Wed 11am PT) and an operational review at the end of week 3.

Ask: can you confirm who from Northgate will be the primary SRE and the procurement contact for access requests? Also flag any compliance constraints (data retention, regions) that might affect dashboards or logging.

Next steps from our side: Logan will own the dashboard templates and onboarding checklist; Marcus will own tracing hook guidance and alert tuning recommendations.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Laura / Marcus —

I uploaded a first-pass ownership grid (attached) and sketched a week-by-week checklist in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-Observability-Onboarding-Northgate. Highlights:

Week 0 (prep, 3–5 days)
- Confirm Okta SSO + SCIM provisioning (Procurement)
- Create Northgate project in Console and grant admin service account
- Share sample load profile and test corpus

Week 1 (instrumentation, 5 days)
- Deploy tracing hooks (client libs + server middleware)
- Validate request-id propagation and KV cache tags
- Import dashboard templates, smoke dashboards up

Week 2 (alerts + taxonomy, 5 days)
- Map errors to taxonomy buckets (client, infra, model, data)
- Tune alert thresholds and route to triage owners
- Draft runbook pages for P1/P2 incidents

Week 3 (operationalize, 5 days)
- Tabletop and runbook rehearsal
- Finalize dashboard permissions and retention
- Post-mortem workflow and handover to SRE rotation

I recommend the first check-in be Wed, Aug 4 at 11am PT to cover Week 0 items and SCIM timing.

Looping in some technical detail so Priya can pre-check with her team.

Tracing hooks:
- Instrumentation libraries: recommend Redwood client v2.3 (auto-instrument for http/grpc) + server middleware for Python/Go.
- Required spans: incoming_request -> model_inference -> model_cache_lookup -> downstream_api_call. Ensure request_id is injected into span tags.
- Sampling: keep adaptive sampling at 5% during load tests, bump to 25% for targeted troubleshooting sessions.

Dashboard templates (attached: dashboard-templates.json)
- API Health (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, throughput)
- Model Quality (prompt failure rate, heuristic scoring)
- Infrastructure (GPU util, memory, disk io)

Error taxonomy draft (short):
- CLIENT_BAD_REQUEST -> frontend team, triage via #northgate-client
- MODEL_TIMEOUT -> ML infra (Marcus), PagerDuty P1
- CACHE_CORRUPTION -> Platform (Priya), PagerDuty P2

Alert routing notes: map P1 to on-call SRE + CS duty; P2 to platform on-call only. See attached alert-routing-diagram.png for a sample flow.

I also put a short runbook template in the Drive folder with steps for containment, mitigation, and postmortem.

— Marcus Lin
Applied ML Engineer | Redwood Inference
